Help, by group.
The station: help moving, help talking, help people.
Making a living: help work, help money, help shops, help ships.
Fun: help casino, help arcade, help events, help hunt, help crews, help duels, help progress.

en.help_moving:
Moving: walk with n, s, e, w, ne, nw, se, sw, u (up) and d (down), or the words: north, south, east, west, northeast, up, down...
look lists the exits; look north peeks next door.
way to the cantina gives the steps from here, compact (2 east, south, then 2 west; a mapper knows more places), and guides you: after each step it says what comes next, finds the way again if you step off it, and says when you've arrived.
guide me to the cantina does the same, guide alone repeats what's left, stop guide ends it.
map describes the deck, where am I names the room and deck, compass your heading.
ride the Wombat flies between the Dock and the Asteroid Belt.
Your cabin is south of the Crew Quarters: invite Maya, then Maya types visit and your name.
Dark tunnels need a headlamp, locked doors a keycard, and outside an EVA suit.
en.help_talking:
Talking: say hello (or start with a quote mark), whisper Maya see you soon (anyone, anywhere), shout hello everyone, gestures like smile, wave, laugh, hug Maya.
who lists who is online, look at Maya describes her, profile Maya shows her progress.
friends, and add friend Maya: with a communicator you hear when friends log in, and locate Maya finds her.
Orbit itself: voices off, speech off, ignore Sam, my voice 3, settings.
en.help_work:
Work: type work at your workplace.
Engineers repeat the reactor's tones in Engineering (the Reactor Core pays more); pilots fly cargo to the Moon from the Dock; traders get a market report anywhere; scientists find the next number in the Science Lab; security officers spot the smuggler in the Cargo Bay.
Answer with the numbers.
Work and missions give XP: levels raise your pay and bring keycards, and rank shows your progress.
The daily mission board: missions, accept 1, take, complete.
Other worlds have work too: type help ships, and see worlds.
en.help_money:
Money: daily gives a bonus once a day, bigger with a streak.
The station's markets each trade their own goods: the Spice Market, west of Hydroponics (coffee, spices, crops); the Ice Depot, north of the Cargo Bay (comet ice, helium-3, frost pearls); the Mineral Exchange, north of the Dock (ores, meteorites); and the Workshop's parts counter (salvage, memory chips).
At a market, prices (or list) says what it buys and sells, at its prices: buy 2 coffee, sell all ore.
Anywhere else, prices coffee names the nearest market for coffee and the way there; the signpost on the Promenade shows them all.
The farm in Hydroponics: plots, plant tomato, water, harvest; crops grow in real time, from ten minutes to a day.
Mining at the Asteroid Belt: ride the Wombat from the Dock, then mine; the Asteroid Surface and the Crystal Cave are richer.
Salvage outside the hull with collect.
Credits are only for playing: they have no real-money value, and can't be bought or cashed out.
Second Orbit, on the Mall Ring, buys back your things for part of their price.
Each world has its own market and prices: trade runs between worlds (help ships).
en.help_shops:
Shops: Star Supply on the East Promenade sells the basics (a mapper, a headlamp, a beacon, a big bag, seeds, snacks).
The Mall Ring, up the lift from the Upper Deck, has Gearworks (devices, keycards, the EVA suit, drills and job tools), Orbit Outfitters (clothes and titles), Cosy Corner (furniture for your cabin), Whiskers & Widgets (pets), the Food Court, and Second Orbit, which buys your things back.
The Cantina's bar sells iced coffee and snacks; Hydroponics sells seeds.
Prices move a little every day, and each shop has a special.
list shows what's for sale, buy mapper buys, examine mapper says what it does.
use X uses a thing (drink, eat, place beacon); wear X and remove X for a headlamp, an EVA suit, clothes or a title.
To trade with another player: offer Sam 3 iron for 200 credits, and they accept or decline.
en.help_admin:
Admin commands: grant Sam 500, take credits Sam 100, give item Sam headlamp, economy, set price coffee 20 (for an hour), reset streak Sam, go to the Bridge or goto Sam, invisible, transfers, revoke Sam, transfer code for Sam, admin log; mute Sam 10, unmute, kick, ban, unban, announce followed by the text.
Events: start event meteor shower (or start event tournament), stop event (or stop event and its name), schedule event 2026-09-27 14:00 and a message (UTC), or schedule event 30 and a message (in 30 minutes).
The hunt: hunt status, new season (reloads the season file), release hint 2, hunt test (play it without counting).
Admins don't count on the hunt's board or for its prizes.
Crews: disband crew and its name.
Duels: stop duel Sam (the stakes go back).
Families: end partnership Sam (for players who can't).
Weddings: cancel wedding Sam (all the money back).

en.help_ships:
Ships and travel: worlds lists the worlds of the simulation, how far each is, and the fares.
Three ways to travel: the Gate (in the Gate Hall, east of the Upper Lift Lobby; on other worlds, at their port): gate to Karmina, at once, for a fee; the ferry (from the Dock; elsewhere, the port): ferry to Karmina, slow but cheap, leaving every two minutes; or your own ship, bought at the Orbit Shipyard on the Mall Ring and docked in the Hangar west of the Dock: embark, fly to Karmina, disembark, refuel, load 20 ice and unload into your bag, cargo shows the hold, name ship gives it a name, and invite Sam lets a friend embark with you.
Every world buys and sells at its own prices: buy cheap on one, sell dear on another; with your ship docked on the same world, what you buy goes into its hold when your bag is full.
Some worlds' customs search travellers for contraband, and fine them.
en.help_worlds_work: Other worlds: mine helium-3 in the Moon's Helium Tunnels; collect in Karmina's farming domes and on its Rust Flats (a suit), and in Glasir's ice quarry (a suit; the crevasse needs a light too); face the creatures of Evergrove's woods (face moss sprite: a test of wits, nobody gets hurt); and take a gig at Lumina City's Courier Hub to carry parcels across the city.

Weddings: buy a ring at Starglint Jewellers on the Mall Ring, then propose to Sam in the same room; Sam says accept or decline, and a yes makes you engaged.
At the jeweller's wedding desk, book wedding with a hall (the Star Dome Hall, the Jasmine Pavilion, or the castle's Great Hall in Evergrove), a tier (simple, grand or luxurious, from 1,000 to 10,000 credits: richer decorations, music and, at the top, fireworks for the station), a ceremony (starlight: the Way of Starlight's rite with lanterns joined into one light and the star bell; or neutral: vows, a yes and signatures) and a time in station time: book wedding pavilion grand neutral 14:00.
wedding says yours; invite Sam to the wedding; guests say rsvp yes or rsvp no.
Be there on time, both of you: the ceremony waits a little.
In it, light lantern, join the lights, vow and your words, yes and sign, when you're asked.
Guests throw flowers, cheer and clap.
Afterwards: the station hears it, you get a title and a keepsake, and read memory brings the day back.
cancel wedding gives all the money back a day ahead, half of it an hour ahead; wedding schedule lists what's coming.

en.whats_new_12: New in Orbit 1.2: the simulation has residents who aren't players, with their own voices and stories: talk to them (talk to Rocco, in the Cantina; residents lists them all), and they'll remember you. Pets to feed, play with, raise and teach tricks (help pets); families, with partners and a baby to adopt at the Medbay (help family); and weddings, from a ring at Starglint Jewellers on the Mall Ring to the Starlight rite (help weddings). The Lantern Festival now lights a gift for everyone.
en.whats_new_13: New in Orbit 1.3: the station's goods are traded at four markets now, each with its own: the Spice Market, west of Hydroponics (coffee, spices, crops); the Ice Depot, north of the Cargo Bay (comet ice, helium-3, frost pearls); the Mineral Exchange, north of the Dock (ores, meteorites); and the Workshop's parts counter (salvage, memory chips). The signpost on the Promenade shows the way. prices at a market lists that market; anywhere else it names the nearest one. The way to a place now comes in short runs (2 east, then north) and guides you step by step; stop guide ends it.
en.whats_new_14: New in Orbit 1.4: Orbit is played in English now, names and all, and it reads English commands: u is up and d is down, and help lists the rest. The markets: the Spice Market, the Ice Depot, the Mineral Exchange and the Workshop's parts counter. The mining shuttle to the Belt is the Wombat (ride the Wombat), and the cargo shuttle to the Moon is the Dove. Martabak is a stuffed pancake now, and kangkung is water spinach, seeds and all. The residents: Rocco at the Cantina (once Jali), Oskar in Engineering (Harsa), Amara in the Star Dome Hall (Sekar), Felix at Gearworks (Tegar), Priya at Whiskers & Widgets (Nilam), Celeste at Starglint Jewellers (Safira), Captain Mateo at the Dock (Bayu), Soren at night on the Observation Deck (Kelana), Shade in the Bazaar's back alley (Bayang), Dario on the Tournament Stage (Ciko), and about the station Poppy (Laras), Hana (Tari), Gino, and Granny Fern in Evergrove (Rimba). They remember you, and everything you own and have done is still yours.
en.whats_new_15: New in Orbit 1.5: type x here (or what can I do here) for the commands that work in the room you're in, a line each, and x and a name for what you can do with a player, a resident or a thing: x Rocco, x jukebox, x headlamp.
